articleBody:
Planning a bathroom tile or stone renovation goes smoother when you have the site details and product specs lined up before your contractor arrives. Review this checklist to make sure your project stays on schedule and avoids unexpected change orders.

- [ ] Slip resistance rating of floor tile — prevents slick, dangerous surfaces in wet areas when stepping out of the shower.
- [ ] Substrate and floor deflection review — confirms your joists can carry the weight of heavy marble, travertine, or large-format tile without flexing.
- [ ] Waterproofing system specification — ensures a dedicated continuous membrane is specified behind the tile rather than relying on backer board alone.
- [ ] Grout type selection — determines whether you use stain-resistant epoxy or standard cement grout that requires ongoing sealing.
- [ ] Plumbing fixture layout and niche locations — establishes exact heights for shampoo niches, grab bars, and mixing valves before board installation.
- [ ] Trim and edge finishing pieces — confirms you have bullnose, pencil tile, or metal profiles ordered to prevent exposed, raw tile edges.
- [ ] Extra tile inventory ordered — provides a 10% to 15% overage buffer for complex cuts, pattern matching, and future repairs.
- [ ] Dust containment and silica plan — clarifies how the contractor will control airborne dust when cutting stone or ceramic inside your home.

How to use this checklist:
Walk through these items during your initial consultation. Having clear expectations around substrate prep, tile thickness, and drying times ensures you receive an accurate, comprehensive estimate.
